message.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Predicting traffic demand is a crucial problem to saving energy and resource pre‐allocation as well as traffic construction planning. The problem is also challenging owing to its non‐linear changing process and complex spatio‐temporal dependencies. Most existing studies train prediction models on traffic data itself and ignore the impact of exogenous factors, thus leading to unsatisfactory performance. To address this issue, we propose a deep neural network, which utilizes multisource urban data to capture specific geospatial and temporal dependencies, for city‐scale taxi demand forecasting. In terms of time dependency, a temporal guidance block is developed to enhance the correlation between time intervals by incorporating time metadata. To capture the geospatial dependencies, we build three parallel geospatial guidance branches that integrate multiple urban data, including population data, POIs, and road networks, to guide the modeling. Each branch contains a geocontext‐aware convolutional layer for extracting geospatial features and a self‐attention mechanism for capturing long‐range spatial dependencies. Extensive experiments have been conducted to demonstrate the superiority of our model over the existing methods, and the prediction error is 16% lower than the state‐of‐the‐art model. We also explore the sensitivity to its parameters and discuss the contributions and limitations of the proposed method.</jats:p>
title: Spatio‐temporal neural network for taxi demand prediction using multisource urban data
